Name: Shashank Tamaskar
Bio:
Prof Shashank Tamaskar earned his BTech from IIT Bombay in 2005 and completed his MS and PhD in Aeronautics and Astronautics from Purdue University in 2011 and 2014, respectively. After completing his PhD, he worked as a Technical Specialist in the Advanced Controls Research Group at Cummins Inc., where he developed algorithms for state estimation and applied model predictive control techniques to internal combustion engines.

At Plaksha, Prof Tamaskar pursues industry-focused research in Multi-Agent Robotic Path Planning and Control and Flexible Robotic Manipulation, with the long-term vision of advancing the adoption of robotics in India. While countries such as China and South Korea have invested heavily in robotics and automation, India still lags behind. India's robot density is only four industrial robots per 10,000 employees, compared with 732 in China and 2,589 in South Korea. Some of the key challenges associated with automation and robotics for small and medium industries include a lack of flexible technologies, high acquisition and maintenance costs, limited technical support, interoperability with legacy automation equipment, and a shortage of indigenous solutions and trained professionals. He actively seeks partnerships with like-minded individuals to help accelerate the adoption of robotics and automation in pursuit of this long-term vision.
Education: PhD, Purdue University | BTech, IIT Bombay
Research_Summary:
Prior to joining Plaksha, Prof Tamaskar worked as a Research Scientist & Project Manager in Siemens Corporation, where he led a team of robotics and machine learning engineers to work on complex R&D projects related to advanced manufacturing and automation.

The research topic areas included flexible robotic control leveraging the digital twin of the manufacturing process, flexible pick and place operations and interoperability between robotic and manufacturing systems. These projects were funded by the Advanced Robotics in Manufacturing (ARM) Institute, which is a DoD sponsored public-private partnership aimed at improving the adoption of robotics in manufacturing.
Research_Interests: Multi-Agent Robotic Path Planning & Control | Flexible Robotic Control & Manipulation | Robotic autonomy | Vision-based robot navigation

Name: Shashikant Pawar
Bio:
Prof Shashikant Pawar works at the intersection of fluid mechanics, turbulence, and computational and experimental methods. He earned his PhD from the Indian Institute of Science (IISc), Bengaluru, where he investigated buoyancy-driven turbulent flows and their role in transport processes in natural systems. He has also worked on the interaction of turbulence with light propagation, motivated by phenomena observed in atmospheric flows.

His research has evolved towards interdisciplinary problems involving complex fluid flows and their interaction with the environment, technology, and biological systems. His current work combines laboratory experiments, computational modelling, flow visualization, and emerging data-driven and AI/ML methods to understand and predict fluid-flow phenomena. He is particularly interested in translating fundamental fluid-mechanics insights into applications relevant to sustainable systems, the built environment, and accessible engineering education.

His academic and industrial experience spans research, teaching, experimental system development, and engineering practice, providing a balance of fundamental understanding and application-oriented problem solving.
Education: PhD, IISc Bengaluru

Before joining Plaksha, he held Assistant Professor roles at Krea University and Nazareth University in Rochester, New York. Prof Suresh Kumar is a Professor of Mathematics at Plaksha University and Director of the Doctoral Program. He is interested in mathematics education and develops e-notes, video lectures, and AI- and Python-assisted learning modules for students.

Name: Swagata Halder
Bio:
Prof Swagata Halder aims to pursue research in the area of DNA damage response to develop novel therapeutic interventions against cancer. His laboratory expertise lies in Molecular Cell Biology and in vitro Protein Biochemistry.

He earned his DPhil from the University of Oxford, UK, under the supervision of Prof Kristijan Ramadan. During his DPhil research, Prof Halder, along with his colleagues, discovered a new human synProfome, now known as SPARTAN synProfome or Ruijs-Aalfs synProfome. This discovery led to the further characterization of the SPRTN protease in the DNA-protein crosslink repair pathway and subsequently established why SPRTN deficiency leads to premature ageing and early-onset liver cancer.
Education: DPhil, University of Oxford | Institute of Veterinary Pharmacology and Toxicology, University of Zurich, Zurich, Switzerland | Scientist, Institute for Research in Biomedicine (IRB), Bellinzona, Switzerland
Research_Summary: Prof Halder pursued his postdoctoral research as a scientist at the Institute for Research in Biomedicine (IRB), Bellinzona, Switzerland, at Prof Petr Cejka's laboratory. By utilizing in vitro biochemistry, Prof Halder has demonstrated how breast cancer susceptibility protein BRCA2 protects stressed replication forks in a RAD51-dependent manner and showed why a single cancer-associated mutation in BRCA2 renders these cells sensitive to DNA-damaging agents (e.g., PARP inhibitors). His work additionally addressed some key fundamental questions in the DNA repair field and paves the way for further research in this rapidly emerging and therapeutically important field.
Research_Interests: DNA-protein crosslinks repair | Ubiquitin proteasome system in DNA damage response | Replication fork reversal and protection | DNA Repair | DNA Damage Response
Publications_Sample: View Prof Halder's complete list of publications here: | https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=I1ieueUAAAAJ&hl=en

Name: T V Ramanathan
Bio:
Prof T V Ramanathan is a Professor at Plaksha University in Mohali, Punjab, India. He earned his PhD in Statistics from the University of Pune. His academic journey includes significant roles such as Senior Professor, Head of the Department of Statistics, and Director of the School of Mathematical and Computing Sciences at Savitribai Phule Pune University (SPPU). Prof Ramanathan has held teaching and research appointments at institutions including Mississippi State University, USA; the University of Waterloo, Canada; KU Leuven, Belgium; the University of Mauritius; and the University of Botswana.

Prof Ramanathan has supervised more than a dozen PhD students and guided numerous students on their MPhil and Master's projects. He has collaborated with researchers worldwide, reflecting his commitment to advancing statistical knowledge and its application across interdisciplinary domains. His dedication to teaching and research reflects his contributions to the academic community and his passion for Statistics and Data Science.
Education: PhD, University of Pune | PhD in Statistics, University of Pune
Research_Summary:
Prof Ramanathan's research focuses on inference in stochastic processes, financial statistics, and time series analysis. His work addresses complex statistical modelling and inference, with applications in finance and data science.

Name: Tapas Pandit
Bio:
Prof Tapas Pandit is an Assistant Professor at Plaksha. He has extensive experience in communication security, theoretical cryptography, and quantum computing. His research interests broadly lie in modern cryptography, with a particular emphasis on the design of post-quantum cryptographic protocols. He is also interested in the design of quantum money.

Prof Pandit earned his MTech and PhD in Computer Science from the Indian Statistical Institute, Kolkata. His doctoral research focused on the design of predicate-based cryptosystems. As a Postdoctoral Researcher at the Indian Institute of Science, Bengaluru, he worked on quantum computing and the design of post-quantum cryptosystems. For more details about his research and other academic activities, please visit his webpage.

Bio: Prof Vasudha Chopra is an Assistant Professor at Plaksha University. Before joining Plaksha, she served as an Assistant Professor of Economics at the Thapar School of Liberal Arts and Sciences. She earned her PhD from the University of Tennessee, Knoxville, and her Master's degree from the TERI School of Advanced Studies, New Delhi.

Prof Chopra is an experimental and behavioral economist. Her research combines applied microeconomic theory with laboratory and field experiments to study stated-preference survey design, group contests, and goal dynamics in teams, drawing on environmental, organizational, and behavioral economics.

Bio: Prof Vishal Garg is a University Chair Professor and Director of the Indorama Ventures Center for Clean Energy at Plaksha University. His teaching includes building energy simulation, green buildings, and illumination engineering.

Name: Andy Ruina
Bio:
Prof Andy Ruina is a Visiting Professor at Plaksha. His main expertise is in Solid Mechanics and Dynamics with specialties in robotics, biomechanics, friction, collisions, bicycle dynamics and mechanics of legged locomotion. His best known papers are on state-variable friction, energy-efficient walking robots, and bicycle balance.

Prof Ruina has had extended visits to MIT, Helsinki University of Technology (Aalto), the Åland University of Applied Sciences, the Indian Institute of Science in Bengaluru, and the US Geological Survey in Menlo Park, CA.

His teaching has mostly been in Solid Mechanics, Engineering Dynamics and Engineering Math.

Prof Ruina's significant teachers and mentors include William Prager at Brown, James R Rice at Brown, James Dieterich at the USGS, and Jim Papadopoulos (now at T-Omega wind). His contributions to the YouTube channel Veritasium on bicycles, sewing machines, and falling chains have had over 50 million hits.

Together with Plaksha VC Rudra Pratap, Prof Ruina has written a 1000 page textbook on statics and dynamics. Before college he took a gap year in Israel learning Fortran, picking oranges, unloading ships and working on a freighter. For 6 years Prof Ruina ran a community bicycle-repair shop in Ithaca, NY. In recent years he enjoys fixing old sewing machines and sailing an old boat.

Name: Nikhil George
Bio:
Nikhil George is a Visiting Assistant Professor at Plaksha. He works at the intersection of Social Science, Human Decision-Making, and Machine Learning from an applied perspective. His research has spanned the restructuring of occupational skills under technological change and expert judgment under pressure, leveraging recent advances in unstructured data and learned representations to ask questions that were not previously tractable.

Nikhil's work develops measurement frameworks using unstructured data and machine learning to uncover patterns that are otherwise difficult to observe, such as how technological change reshapes occupational skills, how AI adoption shifts workforce needs, and when expert decision-making breaks down.

Nikhil's research spans multiple levels. At the macro level, he studies how technological shocks propagate through labor markets and patterns of adaptation. At the behavioral level, he examines when expert judgment diverges from experience-based evidence. At the applied level, he designs frameworks that enable organizations to make more informed talent decisions using existing data.

He works across a range of contexts, including labor markets, firms, competitive sports, and financial services.

Name: Ramneet Kaur
Bio:
Dr Ramneet Kaur is an Adjunct Faculty at Plaksha. Ramneet is an Advanced Computer Scientist II at SRI International's Computer Science Lab in Menlo Park, where she leads high-stakes AI research at the intersection of safety and autonomy. She currently serves as the Principal Investigator (PI) for DARPA's TIAMAT program, focusing on closing the "sim-to-real" gap to ensure robotic agents can perform complex, day-to-day tasks in the physical world. Her leadership extends to the broader academic community, where she has been appointed Program Chair for AAAI 2025 and Area Chair for UAI 2026, reflecting her standing as a leading voice in the next generation of artificial intelligence.

Dr Ramneet earned her PhD from the University of Pennsylvania in 2023 under the supervision of Prof Insup Lee. Her doctoral research focused on the reliable deployment of AI in safety-critical domains, specifically developing tools to monitor distribution shifts and physical attacks on neural networks. By providing rigorous statistical guarantees on false alarm rates and quantifying performance in novel environments, her work adProfesses the fundamental "assurance gap" that prevents deep learning models from being safely integrated into real-world systems. Her excellence in this field led to her selection as one of the 41 top CPS Rising Stars in the United States in 2023, and Distinguished Paper Award and nominations at the International Conference on Cyber-Physical Systems in 2022, 2023, 2025.

At SRI, her recent technical focus has shifted toward the alignment and reliability of Large Language and Multi-Modal Models. She has pioneered methods for integrating uncertainty quantification into generative AI, ensuring these models remain interpretable and dependable even when deployed in dynamic or unpredictable environments where errors could have severe consequences. Her research is extensively published in top-tier venues including NeurIPS, ICML, AAAI, EMNLP, and HSCC, as well as the ACM Transactions on Cyber-Physical Systems. She has been awarded Spot Awards at SRI for her contributions to the DARPA ANSR program in 2024 and publishing in top-tier AI conferences. Beyond her core research, she applies her expertise to social-impact initiatives, such as leveraging machine learning to classify educational content for early childhood development.
Education: PhD, Computer and Information Science, University of Pennsylvania | MS, Computer and Information Science, University of Pennsylvania | MS, Computer Science and Engineering, Indian Institute of Technology, Kharagpur
Research_Interests: Artificial Intelligence | Trustworthy Machine Learning | Interpretability and Fairness | GenAI and Agentic AI Alignment | Interpretable Generative AI

Name: Abhilasha Sinha
Bio:
Abhilasha Sinha is a guest faculty at Plaksha. Abhilasha is an engineer-turned-business operator with expertise in scaling organizations and developing product strategies across diverse sectors, including consumer technology, SaaS, healthcare, and education, in both India and the United States.

She is currently founding a venture in the behavior change space. Her distinguished career includes leadership roles as Chief Growth Officer at Open Secret, India's leading better-for-you food and beverage brand; Chief of Staff to the CEO at Hike, India's homegrown messaging platform; and Vice President of Strategy and Operations at Elucidata, an advanced AI platform serving researchers in biotechnology and pharmaceutical companies.

Abhilasha Sinha holds an MBA with distinction from Harvard Business School and a BTech in Mechanical Engineering from IIT Delhi, where she received the prestigious Bimla Jain Medal for outstanding all-round performance.

Beyond her professional pursuits, Abhilasha is passionate about global exploration. She has traveled to more than 30 countries and visited over 25 states and Union Territories across India.

Name: Ambika Bisla
Bio:
Ambika Bisla is a Guest Faculty at Plaksha. Ambika is a finance professional with experience across global capital markets, public policy, and entrepreneurship. She holds a BA (Honours) in Economics from Lady Shri Ram College, an MBA from IIM Ahmedabad, and a Master of Financial Engineering from the Haas School of Business at the University of California, Berkeley.

Ambika began her career in global investment banking, working at Morgan Stanley and Lehman Brothers in New York and Hong Kong. She later served as a Technical Advisor to the Department of Financial Services in India's Ministry of Finance, where she worked on public policy and regulatory initiatives for financial institutions. Name: Anuj Kapoor
Bio:
Dr Anuj Kapoor is a guest faculty at Plaksha. He is an Assistant Professor of Marketing at the Robert J. Trulaske, Sr. College of Business. His research focuses on the digital economy, particularly the impact of AI on consumers and society, internet media, digital products and platforms, and video advertising.

He holds a PhD in Business Administration from the University of Utah. Before joining the University of Missouri, Dr Kapoor was a faculty member at the Indian Institute of Management Ahmedabad. In 2022, he received the Marti Mannariah Gurunath Outstanding Teacher Award, a school-wide recognition for teaching excellence in IIM Ahmedabad's flagship PGP program. The award is nominated by MBA students and presented annually to a single instructor.

Dr Kapoor's past consulting and executive education clients include Berger Paints, Tata Finance, the Bureau of Indian Standards, Larsen and Toubro, Tata AIA Life Insurance, DailyRounds, HMEL, YPO, Aavas Financiers, IEEMA, Panasonic, Mercedes-Benz Partenrs and Managers, Tata Motors, HDFC Life, and Max Healthcare.

Name: Bhavish Sood
Bio:
Bhavish Sood is a Guest Faculty at Plaksha. Bhavish is a Fractional Entrepreneur-in-Residence and Guest Faculty at Plaksha University, where he teaches entrepreneurship, corporate strategy, and valuation. He is a General Partner at Modulor Capital, a seed-stage micro-VC fund that invests in early-stage ventures, including DesignX, Rezo, Dhurina, Code Quotient, Botman, Fabrik.Space, Sellergeni, and Intents.Mobi. He also serves on the investment committees of multiple pre-seed investment programs at institutions such as Thapar University, Kurukshetra University, FITT IIT Delhi, Chitkara University, and AIC BIMTECH, Noida.

Before founding Modulor Capital, he served as a General Partner at 37.37 North Capital India LLP, where he focused on Series A investments in companies such as Medimetry, Backpacker Panda, and SalesPro.

Bhavish spent more than a decade at Gartner as a Research Director, advising clients worldwide on software markets and technology trends. Earlier in his career, he held operational roles at Virtusa, Zycus, Plexus Technologies, and Konstruct Systems. His work and insights have been featured in The Wall Street Journal, The Economic Times, Business Line, and Mint. In 2010, ARInsights recognized him as one of the world's top industry analysts.

Name: Sandeep Bhushan
Bio:
Sandeep Bhushan is a Visiting Faculty at XLRI and Guest Faculty at Plaksha University, where he teaches strategic marketing and entrepreneurship.

Sandeep brings more than 25 years of experience across corporate India, having worked with leading Indian and global companies. As India Director for the Meta Business Group, he led Meta for Business operations in India. Earlier in his career, he produced consumer brands and go-to-market strategies at Unilever and served as Director of Marketing at Samsung. At the Hindustan Times Group, he was a founding member and Chief Operating Officer of Mint, the business news publication.

Sandeep currently serves on the board of a consumer health company and is a Partner at Social Venture Partners. He has also served on the boards of the Advertising Standards Council of India and the Mobile Marketing Association, where he helped accelerate digital adoption and advance key industry standards.

Name: Seema Bansal
Bio:
Seema Bansal is a Guest Faculty at Plaksha. She is the Vice Chairperson of the Punjab Development Commission, a policy institution established by the Government of Punjab along the lines of NITI Aayog. Since assuming the role in November 2023, Seema has led the Commission's establishment and growth, working closely with the political leadership and bureaucracy to advance Punjab's development priorities, including fiscal management, economic growth, education, healthcare, and agriculture. Under her leadership, the Commission has grown into a 30-member organization with 15 external partnerships spanning nonprofits and think tanks.

Prior to joining the Commission, Seema spent more than 23 years at Boston Consulting Group (BCG), where she led the firm's Social Impact practice in India and across Asia Pacific. She is widely recognized for pioneering the concept of social impact consulting within BCG and across India. During her tenure, Seema worked extensively with central and state governments, including NITI Aayog, the Ministries of Skill Development and Education, and the governments of Haryana, Delhi, Punjab, Rajasthan, Sikkim, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, and Odisha. She has also collaborated with foundations, development organizations, and multilateral institutions.

Profawing on her experience across consulting and government, Seema brings the speed, rigor, and execution-oriented mindset of the private sector to the large-scale and complex challenges of public governance.

Beyond her policy and impact work, Seema is deeply passionate about teaching and mentoring young people. She has previously served as Guest Faculty at Ashoka University and as faculty at the Indian School of Business, Mohali.

Seema is also an acclaimed global speaker, with multiple TED and TEDx Talks that have collectively garnered nearly two million views.

Research_Interests: Social Impact & Development | Public Policy

Name: Somveer Anand
Bio:
Somveer Anand is a Guest Faculty at Plaksha. Somveer serves as CEO and Managing Director of The Innovation Mission Punjab, a Punjab government-supported startup accelerator and pollinator aimed at rejuvenating the state's entrepreneurial spirit and helping scale companies building in Punjab.

From 2016 to 2020, Somveer spent four years building Pindfresh, an agri-tech company. His work experience includes stints at Citibank and Maruti Udyog. Prior to returning to India, Somveer's last engagement was with Avendus Capital in the United States. He has been based in New York, New Delhi, Mumbai, and Kochi before moving to Chandigarh.

Name: Abhay Sharma
Bio: Abhay Sharma is the Registrar at Plaksha University. As Registrar, Abhay brings over four decades of distinguished experience spanning industry and higher education. A strategic leader with expertise in university administration, he has played pivotal roles in establishing and scaling multiple educational institutions. His comprehensive experience encompasses statutory compliance, operational excellence, and institutional development. Throughout his career, he has demonstrated exceptional prowess in strategic planning, regulatory affairs, and building robust administrative frameworks. Prior to joining Plaksha, he held senior leadership positions at several prestigious institutions, including the University of Petroleum and Energy Studies, Dehradun; KR Mangalam University, Gurugram; BML Munjal University, Gurugram and Nayanta Education Foundation, Hyderabad, where he consistently drove operational excellence and institutional growth. A dynamic leader known for his analytical mindset and team-oriented approach, Sharma has consistently demonstrated success in creating efficient, sustainable work environments that advance organizational missions. His unique blend of industrial and academic experience, coupled with his proven track record in human relations and strategic operations management, makes him invaluable in driving Plaksha's administrative excellence. Throughout his 25-year tenure in leadership positions, he has championed operational efficiency while maintaining the highest standards of regulatory compliance and institutional governance.

Name: Arvind Agrawal
Bio: Arvind Agrawal has 35+ years of extensive international management experience across American Express, IBM and Concentrix in senior executive leadership positions. He is very passionate about developing the next generation of leaders and has mentored over 200+ leaders throughout his journey. Most recently at Concentrix, he served as SVP & GM of the Asia Pacific business, where he was responsible for approximately $500M+ Profit & Loss and more than 200 clients, and drove rapid growth, both organically and inorganically, across 13 countries. Additionally, he was also the Global Exec Sponsor of Network of Women, a company-wide D&I initiative focused on encouraging more women in senior leadership. Prior to Concentrix, at IBM, Arvind rebuilt the foundation of an underperforming outsourcing F&A business and set it up for aggressive growth, doubling the revenue within less than 3 years and growing the team size to more than 5000 employees. Following this, he took on the responsibility to turn around IBM’s BPO portfolio across all key Growth Markets, including Asia Pacific, LATAM and CE Europe. He was also a key member of the handpicked global task force that helped divest IBM's customer service BPO business to Concentrix.

Name: Dr. Rajesh Nair
Bio: Dr Rajesh Nair is a Founder of Plaksha University. He is one of the Co-founders of Indegene, and the President of the company. His work includes developing new strategic initiatives, especially as they relate to the company's solutions in RWD-driven R&D for the life sciences. He comes with 24 years of experience in the technology-led healthcare solutions provider sector. Dr Nair headed the bio-tech division of the Sarabhai Group before co-founding Indegene. He earned his MBBS from GMC Thiruvananthapuram, India (1993) and is also a physician by training. Post that, he pursued an MBA from IIM Ahmedabad. During his time at IIM Ahmedabad, he was also a member of the Entrepreneurship Club and the IIM Ahmedabad Quiz Club.

Name: M Balakrishnan
Bio:
Prof M Balakrishnan is a Senior Advisor, Faculty Affairs at Plaksha University. He joined Plaksha as a Visiting Faculty after more than three decades in the CSE Department at IIT Delhi. He has held various leadership positions, including Dean(Post Graduate Studies & Research), Deputy Director (Faculty) and Deputy Director (Strategy & Planning). At IIT Delhi, he has been responsible for numerous initiatives related to industry-academia partnerships, institutional collaborations, curriculum, society outreach as well as administrative reforms.  He continues to be an Honorary Professor in the CSE Department at IIT Delhi. His research interests are in Embedded Systems Design, Electronic Design Automation and Assistive Technology. He has been a pioneer in Assistive Technology research in India and has received three National awards as well as the ACM Eugene L Lawler Award. He founded the ASSISTECH lab at IIT Delhi as well as the EMPOWER Assistive Technology conference. He is a fellow of ACM as well as INAE.

Prof Balakrishnan's research interests include assistive technologies, embedded systems, EDA and system-level design. He founded the ASSISTECH laboratory along with Prof. PVM Rao (Mech Engg Department) nearly 15 years ago, which is focused on mobility and education for visually impaired people. The lab has consistently worked towards building affordable assistive technology solutions that address the needs of our infrastructure and society. ASSISTECH successes include SmartCane as well as a non-profit startup, Raised Lines Foundation, which is dedicated to supporting STEM education for visually impaired people by developing tactile diagrams and kits.

Name: Rishi Nath Khanna
Bio: Rishi Nath Khanna is a Founding Donor and Changemaker at Plaksha University. An alumnus of IIT Delhi, he is an entrepreneur and industry leader who has contributed as a Changemaker towards the vision, endowment, and development of Plaksha University.

Name: S Shankar Sastry
Bio: Prof S Shankar Sastry is the Founding Chancellor of Plaksha University. He is currently the Thomas Siebel Distinguished Professor of Computer Science. He was till 2022 also the Director of the Blum Center for Developing Economies, a Center spanning the ten campuses of the University of California, dedicated to the use of technology and innovative business models to lift people out of poverty. He is also the Co-Director of the C3 Digital Transformation Institute (C3DTI), a data sciences institute spanning Berkeley, UIUC, CMU, Chicago, MIT, Princeton, Royal Institute of Technology, Stockholm, and Stanford. C3DTI is an institute aimed to develop the science and technology of digital transformation in societal systems such as in health care, energy systems, transportation systems. Additionally, he has helped launch a new FHL Vive Center for Enhanced Reality for exploring the boundaries between augmented reality and real scenes with applications to autonomy, performance arts, and education. He has faculty appointments in the departments of Electrical Engineering and Computer Sciences, Bioengineering and Mechanical Engineering. From 2007 to 2018, he was the Dean and Roy W Carlson Professor of Engineering. From 2004 to 2007 he was the Director of CITRIS (Center for Information Technology in the Interests of Society), an interdisciplinary center spanning UC Berkeley, Davis, Merced and Santa Cruz. He has served as Chairman, Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Sciences, University of California, Berkeley from January, 2001 through June 2004. From 1999-2001, he was the Director of the Information Technology Office at the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) in Arlington, VA. Prof Sastry received his PhD degree in 1981 from the University of California, Berkeley. He was on the faculty of MIT as Asst. Professor from 1980-82 and Harvard University as a Gordon McKay Professor in 1994. His areas of personal research are AI and Machine Learning, resilient cyber-physical systems, mechanism design and incentive theory for the digital transformation system of complex societal scale systems networks, cybersecurity, autonomous robotic vehicles and robots, computer vision, nonlinear and adaptive control, control of hybrid and embedded systems. He is also deeply committed to the use of technology to lift people out of poverty as testified by his work with USAID, PhilDev, and other international foundations through his directorship of the Blum Center for Developing Economies. From 2006 to 2017, he led a ten-year NSF Science and Technology Center (with multi-university partners), TRUST (Team for Research in Ubiquitous Secure Technologies) and its successor five-year center 2013-19, FORCES (Foundations of Resilient Cyber Physical Systems). He has co-authored about 600 technical papers. He has co-authored or co-edited 10 books, including Adaptive Control: Stability, Convergence and Robustness (with M Bodson, Prentice Hall, 1989) and A Mathematical Introduction to Robotic Manipulation (with R Murray and Z Li, CRC Press, 1994), Nonlinear Systems: Analysis, Stability and Control (Springer-Verlag, 1999), and An Invitation to 3D Vision: From Images to Models (Springer Verlag, 2003) (with Y Ma, S Soatto, and J Kosecka) and Generalized Principal Component Analysis (Springer Verlag, 2016 with R Vidal and Y Ma). Prof Sastry served as Associate Editor for numerous publications, including: IEEE Transactions on Automatic Control; IEEE Control Magazine; IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems; the Journal of Mathematical Systems, Estimation and Control; IMA Journal of Control and Information, International Journal of Adaptive Control and Signal Processing; Journal of Biomimetic Systems and Materials, the IEEE Proceedings. Prof Sastry was elected to the National Academy of Engineering in 2001 the American Academy of Arts and Sciences in 2004, Fellow of IEEE in 1994, and International Federation of Automatic Control Fellow in 2016. He received the President of India Gold Medal in 1977, the IBM Faculty Development in 1983, the NSF Presidential Young Investigator Award in 1985. He got the Eckman Award of the American Automatic Control Council in 1990, the Ragazzini Award for Distinguished Accomplishments in teaching in 2005 and the Rufus Oldenburger Carrer Award of ASME in 2021.. He received an MA (honoris causa) from Harvard in 1994, an honorary PhD from KTH, the Royal Institute of Technology, Stockholm in 2007, an honorary PhD from the Royal Institute of Technology, Stockholm in 2008, a PhD Honoris causa from the University of Waterloo, Canada in 2016, and a Laurea Dottorato honoris causa (honorary doctorate) from Politecnico di Torino in 2018, and the Berkeley Citation in 2018. He has also received the distinguished Alumnus Award of the Indian Institute of Technology in 1999, the International House at UC Berkeley, and the David Marr prize for the best paper at the International Conference in Computer Vision in 1999. He has been a member of the Air Force Scientific Advisory Board from 2002 to 2005 and the Defense Science Board in 2008 among other national boards. He has been on the Scientific Advisory Boards of the National Science Foundation, Engineering Directorate, Lockheed Martin Corporation and the United Nations Secretary General, the World Economic Forum Global Development Council, Interwest LLC, and Eriksholm Otticon. He is currently on the corporate boards of C3.ai, HCL Technologies, and Lexmark Corporation. He has supervised about 70 doctoral students and over 50 MS students to completion, as well as over 30 post-doctoral scholars. His former advisees occupy leadership roles on the faculties of many major universities in the United States and abroad.
